question: A chord of length 8 cm is 3 cm from the center. Find the radius.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **radius**, **distance from the center**, and **half of the chord** always form a right-angled triangle.

Half of the chord = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.

Using the standard **Pythagorean triplet** (3, 4, 5):

If the two sides are 3 cm and 4 cm, the hypotenuse (radius) must be 5 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Length of **chord (AB)** = 8 cm, **Distance from center (OM)** = 3 cm.

**Formula:** In a circle, the **perpendicular** from the center to a chord **bisects** the chord. **Radius² = (Half-chord)² + (Distance)²**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c830a39cd84ecdecc9f2a40f5ea5d0ecd0c661170ae8dae061cdbbebd75904b.png] 

⇒ Let **O** be the center and **AB** be the chord.

⇒ **OM** ⊥ **AB**, so **AM = MB = AB ÷ 2**

⇒ **AM** = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm

⇒ In right Δ**OMA**, **OA² = OM² + AM²**

⇒ **Radius²** = 3² + 4²

⇒ **Radius²** = 9 + 16 = 25

⇒ **Radius** = √25 = 5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Bisector Property

The perpendicular drawn from the **center** of a circle to a **chord** bisects the chord into two equal segments.

Pythagorean Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, **Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²**. Common triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17).

Diameter and Radius Relation

The **diameter** of a circle is the longest chord and its length is exactly **2 × radius**.

Equal Chords Property

Chords of equal length are **equidistant** from the center of the circle.</p
